description:
347 tiles at 16x16 for a harbour village on a sunny coast: beach sand, the sea with a surf line along the shore, red-earth terraces on the hill, a stone quay standing in the water, whitewashed houses under terracotta roofs, olive trees, parasols, rowboats and a windmill whose sails turn. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 235 of the 347 tiles are transitions, 68% of the pack. 5 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a set missing three tiles is broken in your map.
  • A house you paint to any shape. The terracotta roof is a faced set: paint it as a mass on the terrace or on the quay and its south wall draws itself, whitewashed with blue shutters. Every roof tile is declared blocked in tiles.json, because a house is walked round.
  • A quay that stands in the water. The quay stone is a faced set too: its wall drops to a dark wet foot at the waterline. The quay is walkable, except along that face.
  • A shore and terraces. The sea meeting the beach, with a pale surf line, and the red-earth terraces on the sand, each with its own set and a soft organic edge. Every sea tile is declared blocked.
  • 5 materials × 4 variants, the three walking grounds on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so the terrace earth, the quay stone and the sand never merge into one warm field. The smallest gap on the ladder is 23.3 luma, measured from the shipped pixels rather than declared.
  • 19 objects across 44 prop tiles plus the animation frames: an olive tree, a lemon tree in a terracotta pot, geraniums in a painted tin, bougainvillea, a prickly pear, a rowboat drawn up on the beach, a heap of blue net with its floats, a crate of the morning catch, a lobster pot, an anchor, a mooring bollard with its rope, a whitewashed well, a stone bench, a cafe table with two chairs, a striped beach parasol and a striped deck chair. Each ships transparent, and grounded on its floor with the contact shadow drawn.
  • 3 animated objects, 48 frames: a windmill whose four sails turn and loop exactly, a blue and white harbour flag that waves, and a harbour light that glows. No two frames of a set are the same picture.
  • A finished 40x28 sample map with 88 objects on it and every autotile set placed, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 20 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 417 files in total, and a tiles.json giving every tile's role, material, sheet slot, footprint and passability.

Three things to know before you buy

⚠️ Keep the quay in the water. The quay set draws sea outside its edge, so a quay laid straight against the beach shows a strip of water along the join. On the sample map it leaves the map on the east and south, where its land lies. There are no people or animals in the pack.

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the windmill, the flag and the harbour light arrive as static frames on page C.

⚠️ At 347 tiles it is a smaller pack than most of the series, and it is priced for that.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ: an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 5 of 5 sets, 235 of 235 masked tiles, and 240 of 240 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame.
  • Tiled: one .tsx per group, all 9 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 500 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 1,146,880 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4: a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 9 atlas sources, 347 of 347 declared tiles built, 57 of 57 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 81 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete: exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

The autotile sets

  • sea_on_sand
  • terrace_on_sand
  • quay_on_sea
  • roof_on_terrace
  • roof_on_quay

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this coast sits beside the others and a map can run straight out of it into another pack.

  • Verdant 10 — Harbour — a working harbour to run the quay into
  • Verdant 23 — Ruins — classical ruins, amphorae and cypresses for the hill above the village
  • Verdant 09 — Town — the town inland: its market, housefronts and gardens

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance. No diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
